title: Organometallics and Catalysis
tagline: Electron counting, main-group and transition-metal organometallics, elementary reactions, catalytic cycles, cross-coupling, metathesis and heterogeneous catalysis
summary: Organometallic compounds, with bonds between metals and carbon, are the workhorses of modern catalysis. This course covers electron counting and the common ligands, main-group organometallic reagents, the elementary reactions of transition-metal complexes, and how they combine into catalytic cycles for hydrogenation, cross-coupling, metathesis and polymerisation, ending with catalysis on surfaces.

chapters.title: Organometallic compounds and electron counting
chapters.summary: Metal–carbon bonds, electron counting and the 18-electron rule, and σ-donor and π-acceptor ligands.

chapters.title: Main-group organometallic reagents
chapters.summary: Organolithium and Grignard reagents, organozinc, organoboron and organosilicon compounds, and their uses in synthesis.

chapters.title: Carbonyls, phosphines, alkenes and other ligands
chapters.summary: Metal carbonyls and their infrared signatures, phosphines, and alkene, alkyne, carbene, cyclopentadienyl and arene ligands.

chapters.title: Elementary reactions
chapters.summary: Ligand substitution, oxidative addition and reductive elimination, migratory insertion and β-hydride elimination.

chapters.title: Catalytic cycles: hydrogenation and hydroformylation
chapters.summary: Building catalytic cycles from elementary steps, Wilkinson’s catalyst, asymmetric hydrogenation and hydroformylation.

chapters.title: Cross-coupling reactions
chapters.summary: Palladium-catalysed Suzuki, Heck, Sonogashira and Buchwald–Hartwig couplings and their mechanisms.

chapters.title: Metathesis and polymerisation catalysis
chapters.summary: Alkene metathesis with Grubbs and Schrock catalysts, and Ziegler–Natta and metallocene catalysts for polymerising alkenes.

chapters.title: Heterogeneous catalysis
chapters.summary: Active sites on metal surfaces, supported catalysts, zeolites and oxides, and how working catalysts are characterised.
